# Angular conventions (Angular 22, standalone, zoneless)

## Folder layout (feature-first)
```
frontend/src/app/
  core/                 # app-wide singletons: country context, http, error handling
  shared/ui/            # reusable presentational components (no business logic)
  features/<feature>/   # one folder per feature, e.g. country-selection, quote-form, plan-list, summary
    <feature>.page.ts   # routed container component
    components/         # presentational components of this feature
    data/               # API service + models (*.model.ts) + mappers
    state/              # signal-based store for the feature, if needed
    *.spec.ts           # tests next to the code they test
```

## Components
- Standalone only, `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`, no NgModules.
- `input()`, `output()`, `model()` signal APIs; `inject()` instead of constructor injection.
- Templates use `@if`, `@for` (always with `track`), `@switch`. No `*ngIf` / `*ngFor`.
- Container (page) components talk to services/state; presentational components only receive inputs and emit outputs.
- Every async view handles three states: loading, error (with retry), empty.

## State
- `signal()` / `computed()` for state; `linkedSignal()` / `resource()` / `httpResource()` when they simplify async data.
- RxJS only where streams are genuinely needed (e.g. debounced input). Convert at the edge with `toSignal()`.
- Wizard state that must survive back-navigation or refresh lives in one store per wizard, persisted to `sessionStorage` through a single persistence helper. Never store tokens there.

## HTTP and contracts
- Call only relative URLs (`/api/...`). No hosts, no tokens, no `environment.ts` secrets.
- Strapi responses are mapped to app models in `data/*.mapper.ts`; components never see raw Strapi shapes.
- Models mirror the Strapi schema (source of truth). Any schema change updates the model in the same commit.

## Forms
- Typed Reactive Forms (`FormGroup<{...}>`, `nonNullable`) or Signal Forms if stable in the installed version — decided once in the plan, then consistent.
- Dynamic form: config from CMS → typed field descriptors → validators built by a pure function (`buildValidators(field)`) that is unit-tested per rule.
- Error messages come from configuration, shown next to the field, linked with `aria-describedby`.

## Accessibility (mandatory)
- Every control has a visible `<label for>`; help text and errors linked via `aria-describedby`; invalid fields get `aria-invalid="true"`.
- The whole wizard is operable by keyboard; on step change, move focus to the step heading.
- Use native elements (`button`, `input`, `select`) before ARIA roles.

## Styling
- BEM class names: `block__element--modifier`. SCSS per component; design tokens as CSS custom properties in `styles.scss`.
- Mobile-first; layouts must work from 320px width.

## Testing
- Vitest unit tests for: validators, mappers, price rules, stores, critical component interactions.
- No tests for styles, static templates or scaffolding.
- Name tests after requirements: `describe('US-01 · FR-003 vehicle year range', ...)`.
- Prefer testing pure functions; for components use `TestBed` with harness-free DOM queries by role/label.

# Strapi conventions (Strapi 5, TypeScript, SQLite)

## Content types live in code
- Every content type and component is defined as schema files under `cms/src/api/<name>/content-types/<name>/schema.json` and `cms/src/components/<category>/<name>.json`.
- Never rely on changes made only through the admin Content-Type Builder: they are not reviewable. If one is made in dev, commit the generated files.
- Use `draftAndPublish: true` for business-managed content so only published entries reach the app.
- Field names in camelCase; descriptive names (`basePrice`, not `price1`).

## Country differentiation
- The strategy is defined in the multi-country ADR in `docs/adr/`. Read it before modelling any content type and follow it exactly. Do not introduce a second mechanism.

## Querying (Strapi 5)
- Server code uses the Document Service API: `strapi.documents('api::x.x').findMany({ filters, populate, status: 'published' })`.
- REST responses in Strapi 5 are flat (no `data.attributes`); entries are identified by `documentId`.
- Populate explicitly what the frontend needs; never `populate=*` in production paths.

## Security and permissions
- The browser only reads. The Public role gets `find` / `findOne` on exactly the content types the wizard reads — nothing else, no `create/update/delete`.
- Permissions are granted in code at bootstrap (`cms/src/index.ts`), so a fresh database is configured identically. List each granted action with a comment saying why.
- No API tokens are created by code. No token of any kind reaches the frontend.
- Never read, print or commit `.env`; document new variables in `.env.example` only.

## Seed data
- Seed runs at bootstrap only when the database is empty, is idempotent, and lives in `cms/src/seed/` (one file per content type, data per country).
- Fictitious data only (no real people, documents or plates).
- Seeded entries are published so the app works right after `docker compose up`.
- An admin user for local development may be created from `.env` variables; defaults are dev-only and documented in the README.

## Contract
- The schema is the source of truth for the API contract. When a field is added/removed/renamed, report it so the Angular models in `frontend/src/app/features/*/data/` are updated in the same commit.
- Breaking changes to an existing contract require human approval (constitution §3.3).

## Verification
- `npm --prefix cms run build` must pass before reporting.

# UI/UX guidelines

Visual language derived from research of the public car-insurance sites of a reference LatAm insurer operating in Colombia and Chile (2026-11-21). We reuse its **patterns and token values**, never its assets: no third-party logos, fonts or images in the repo. The product is a fictitious insurtech with its own text wordmark.

## 1. Design tokens

Defined once as CSS custom properties in `frontend/src/styles.scss`. Components use tokens only — no raw hex values.

```scss
:root {
  /* Brand */
  --color-brand: #0033a0;          /* navy: header, wordmark, info */
  --color-action: #2d6df6;         /* buttons, links, plan names */
  --color-action-hover: #26328c;
  --color-cta: #e3e829;            /* main CTA background only */
  --color-cta-hover: #d7de17;
  --color-on-cta: #26328c;         /* text on yellow */
  --color-accent: #00aec7;         /* DECORATIVE ONLY, never text (2.7:1) */

  /* Text & surfaces */
  --color-text: #1c1c24;
  --color-text-muted: #53565a;
  --color-surface: #ffffff;
  --color-surface-alt: #f8f8f8;    /* cards */
  --color-surface-highlight: #dfeaff; /* recommended plan, badges */
  --color-border: #cdced9;
  --color-disabled-bg: #e7e7e7;
  --color-disabled-text: #666666;   /* 4.6:1 on disabled-bg (Sura's #878789 was 2.9:1) */

  /* Status (fg / bg) */
  --color-error: #d12d35;   --color-error-bg: #fff4f3;
  --color-success: #067014; --color-success-bg: #def6de;
  --color-warning: #ed8b00; --color-warning-bg: #fff5ec;
  --color-info: #0033a0;    --color-info-bg: #e0eaff;

  /* Spacing (4px base) */
  --space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 12px; --space-4: 16px;
  --space-6: 24px; --space-8: 32px; --space-12: 48px;

  /* Radius */
  --radius-sm: 8px;      /* inputs */
  --radius-md: 16px;     /* cards */
  --radius-pill: 999px;  /* buttons, badges */

  /* Elevation */
  --shadow-card: 0 4px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.16);
  --shadow-soft: 0 8px 25px rgba(83, 89, 144, 0.07);
  --focus-ring: 0 0 0 4px rgba(0, 56, 255, 0.22);
}
```

## 2. Typography

- **Font:** Figtree from the Google Fonts CDN, only the weights we use, with `display=swap`:
  ```html
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Figtree:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  ```
- **Fallback (lightweight, no download):** `--font-family: 'Figtree', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;`
- **Scale (mobile → desktop):**

| Role | Size | Weight | Color |
|------|------|--------|-------|
| Price / hero heading | 32px → 48px | 700 | `--color-text` |
| Step heading (`h1`) | 24px → 32px | 700 | `--color-brand` |
| Section / card title | 20px | 700 | `--color-action` |
| Body | 16px, line-height 1.5 | 400 | `--color-text` |
| Label, badge, helper | 14px | 500 | `--color-text-muted` |

- Never below 14px. Blue text (`--color-action`) only at ≥16px.

## 3. Component recipes (BEM)

Each component defines: default, hover, focus-visible, disabled and (if applicable) error/selected states.

**Button** — `.button`, `.button--cta`, `.button--primary`, `.button--secondary`
- Pill (`--radius-pill`), min-height 48px, padding `--space-3 --space-6`, 16px / 700.
- `--cta`: yellow bg, navy text. One per screen: the step's main action (Continue, Pay).
- `--primary`: action-blue bg, white text, hover `--color-action-hover`.
- `--secondary`: white bg, 1px navy border (Back, Edit).
- Disabled: `--color-disabled-bg` / `--color-disabled-text` (≥ 4.5:1), plus `aria-disabled` or `disabled`. Loading: keep width, show spinner + "Procesando…", `aria-busy="true"`.

**Choice tile** — `.choice-tile`, `--selected`: large single-choice option (e.g. country). Native radio inside a `<label>`.
- Default: `--color-surface`, 2px `--color-border`, `--radius-md`, min-height 96px, flag above name, name 20px/700 `--color-text` (black, never brand or white).
- Hover: border `--color-action` only. Never a background change or dark fill.
- Selected: 2px `--color-action` border + bg `--color-surface-highlight` + check icon absolutely positioned in the top-right corner (not color alone; no extra text, so selecting causes no layout shift). The native radio announces the checked state.
- Focus: `--focus-ring`. All text states ≥ 4.5:1.

**Form field** — `.form-field`, `__label`, `__control`, `__help`, `__error`, `--invalid`
- Label above the control, 14px/500; required marked with `*` and announced (`required` attribute).
- Control (soft filled, chosen at US-01 Gate 2): min-height 52px, 16px text (prevents iOS zoom), `--color-surface-brand-soft` fill, 12px top radius, no side borders, 2px bottom line `--color-text-muted` (≥3:1 against the fill). Focus: bottom line `--color-action`, fill `--color-surface-field-focus` (`#e8f0ff`), plus `--focus-ring` on `:focus-visible`. Invalid: bottom line `--color-error`.
- Placeholder only as an example (`Ej: ABC123`), never as the label.
- Error: icon + text in `--color-error` below the control, `aria-describedby` linked, `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
- **Select** (`.select-field`): never the native option list. A `role="combobox"` trigger with the same soft-filled look and a chevron that rotates when open, plus a `role="listbox"` popup: white, 14px radius, `--shadow-card`, 6px padding; options 10px/12px padding, 10px radius, `--color-surface-brand-soft` for the active option, selected option bold `--color-on-cta` with a check icon. Keyboard per the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox: ↑/↓, Home/End, Enter/Space to pick, Esc to close, Tab to leave; `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`.
- Yes/No and short choices: segmented toggle built on native radio inputs (`.segmented`, `__option`, `--checked`).

**Form card** — `.form-card`: `--color-surface`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`, padding `--space-6`, max-width 560px, centered. Title 20px/700 `--color-action`.

**Plan card** — `.plan-card`, `__badge`, `__radio`, `__name`, `__price`, `__section`, `__item`, `--recommended`, `--selected` (agreed at US-02 Gate 2)
- White `--color-surface`, 14px radius, padding `--space-4`/`--space-6`, 1px inset ring `--color-border`. No top stripe and no grey background.
- `--recommended`: a 5px `--color-brand` top border, a 1px brand ring, and a large `__badge` pill ("Recomendado" with a star icon; 16px bold text, an 18px icon, 6px × 18px padding; `--color-cta` bg, `--color-on-cta` text) centred **on the top border**. Only the first recommended plan in order.
- `--selected`: a `__radio` circle filled with `--color-action` and a white check, plus a 2px **inset** `--color-action` ring. No "Seleccionado" text: nothing may change size or position (no layout shift). The radio state is the non-colour cue.
- The cards share one CSS subgrid, so the name and description, the price (after a divider), Coberturas and Beneficios start on the same line in every card.
- Price: large, `--color-brand`, formatted in the country's currency with no decimals, followed by "/ mes". No text explaining how the price is calculated.
- Sections: Coberturas and Beneficios with check icons; an empty list is hidden.
- Selectable as a radio group, one choice only; the arrow keys move the choice.
- The "Continuar" pill is disabled (`--color-disabled-bg` / `--color-disabled-text`) until a plan is chosen, with no hint text.

**Stepper** — `.stepper`, `__step`, `--current`, `--done`: numbered steps with text labels in an `<ol>`, above the form card; current step has `aria-current="step"`. Current and done circles (32px): `--color-surface-highlight` fill, 2px `--color-action` ring, `--color-brand` number (check icon when done); upcoming: white, 1.5px `--color-border` ring, `--color-text-muted`. Current label bold `--color-brand`; connector lines 2px, `--color-action` up to a done step, else `--color-border`. On mobile show only the current circle + "Paso 2 de 3" + current label.

**Motion** — content loads with a skeleton, then items fade up 14px one by one (600ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`, 110ms stagger), only on first render, never on validation re-renders. Popups open with a 160ms fade/slide. All of it is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**Summary block** — `.summary-section` with a title + "Editar" secondary link per section (data, vehicle, plan). Masked document shown as `•••• 5678`.

**States**
- **Loading:** skeletons shaped like the final content (cards, fields); `aria-busy` on the region.
- **Empty** (e.g. no plans): flat illustration or icon, friendly headline, one-line explanation, one action.
- **Error** (e.g. payment rejected, CMS down): `--color-error-bg` panel with icon, what happened, what to do, and a retry button. Never lose user data.
- **Success** (confirmation): `--color-success` check icon, headline, quote number prominent and copyable.

## 4. Accessibility (non-negotiable)

- Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1. `--color-accent` never carries text; white on `--color-action` only at ≥16px bold.
- Visible `:focus-visible` on every interactive element (`--focus-ring`). Never `outline: none` without replacement.
- Touch targets ≥ 48×48px.
- Information never by color alone (selected, recommended, error all have text/icon).
- On step change, move focus to the step heading; announce async errors with `role="alert"`.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no transitions).

## 5. Layout

- Mobile-first. Breakpoints are Bootstrap's: sm 576, md 768, lg 992, xl 1200 px. Custom media queries use the same values.
- **Layouts use Bootstrap 5.3 grid and utilities** ([ADR 0003](../../../docs/adr/0003-bootstrap-grid-for-layouts.md)) on every screen. Bootstrap is for layout only:
  - Page width: every screen's content sits in a `.container`, capped at 1140 px (global override), with Bootstrap's gutters.
  - Structure: `.row` / `.col-*` (`.col-12 .col-md-6`, …) for columns that stack on mobile.
  - Alignment and spacing: `.d-flex`, `.flex-column`, `.justify-content-*`, `.align-items-*`, `.gap-*`, `m-*` / `p-*`, `.text-center` / `.text-md-start`, `.d-none .d-md-block`.
  - Never use Bootstrap colour, typography, border, shadow or component classes (`.btn`, `.card`, `.bg-*`, `.text-primary`, `.fs-*`…). Those come from our tokens and BEM recipes.
  - Component SCSS holds component styling only (look, states, internal spacing with `--space-*`), not page layout.
- Plan cards: a Swiper slider below 992px (about 1.2 cards on mobile, 2.2 on tablet, with previous/next arrows and dots, opening on the recommended plan, no loop and no autoplay; only the load animation); a 3-column grid from 992px.
- Header: navy bar with text wordmark; no navigation beyond the wizard.

## 6. Imagery

- Hero/decoration: optional. If used, fictitious stock-style photos of real-looking people relaxed with car/phone, or flat illustrations with soft blobs in brand blue, yellow and cyan.
- Empty/error states: simple flat illustration or large icon, never a stock photo.
- Decorative images: `alt=""`. Informative images: alt describes the content.
- Only images we are licensed to use (own SVGs, open-licensed illustrations). No assets from third-party sites.

## 7. Copy tone (Spanish, both countries)

- Informal "tú", warm, short sentences. CTAs as actions: "Continuar", "Ver planes", "Pagar ahora".
- Errors say what to do: "Ingresa una placa válida, por ejemplo ABC123."
- Country vocabulary comes from the CMS (placa vs patente, cédula vs RUT) — never hard-code it.

## 8. Design options in plan.md (Gate 2)

For each client-facing view, propose 2–3 options that **vary layout or interaction, not the visual language** (all use these tokens and components). Format per option:

```
### Option A — <name>
- Layout: <one or two lines, mobile and desktop>
- Pros / Cons: <...>
- Accessibility notes: <...>
**Recommendation:** Option X, because <...>
```

Examples of meaningful variations: form in one long card vs. grouped sections (policyholder / vehicle); plan cards side by side vs. comparison table; summary as cards vs. single list with inline edit links.

# Project Context & Rules

Always read and follow `.specify/memory/constitution.md` before planning, writing code, or running commands.
The full agentic flow (steps, gates, agents) is described in `FLOW.md`.

## Repository Structure
- `cms/`: Headless CMS built with Strapi 5 (TypeScript, SQLite). Content types, APIs, seed, permissions.
- `frontend/`: Angular 22 app (TypeScript, ESLint), Vitest unit tests next to the code, Playwright e2e in `frontend/e2e/`.
- `docs/user-stories/`: Functional user stories pasted verbatim by the human (`US-XX.md`). Never edited by AI.
- `docs/adr/`: Architecture Decision Records (MADR), `NNNN-<slug>.md`.
- `specs/NNN-us-XX-<slug>/`: `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `analysis.md`, `review.md` per user story (Spec Kit).
- `.claude/agents/`: subagent definitions. `.claude/skills/`: skills.
- `ai-logs/`: exported agent sessions. Never edit.

## Verification Commands
- **Frontend (lint + typecheck + unit tests):** `npm --prefix frontend run verify`
- **Frontend build:** `npm --prefix frontend run build`
- **Frontend e2e (Playwright):** `npm --prefix frontend run e2e`
- **CMS build / typecheck:** `npm --prefix cms run build`
- **CMS unit tests:** `npm --prefix cms test`
- **CMS dev server:** `npm --prefix cms run develop`
- **Full stack:** `docker compose up --build`

## Stack Rules (all agents)
- **Angular:** standalone components only, no NgModules; signals for state; built-in control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`); typed forms; no `any`. Details: `angular-conventions` skill.
- **Strapi:** schemas defined in code; Public role gets only `find`/`findOne` on what the wizard reads. Details: `strapi-conventions` skill.
- **Security:** no Strapi token of any kind in the frontend; the browser calls only relative `/api/...` URLs (proxied by nginx / `proxy.conf.json`).
- **Layout:** Bootstrap 5.3 grid and utilities only (containers, grid, flex, spacing), never its colour, typography or component classes. Details: `ui-ux-guidelines` skill §5, ADR 0003.
- **Accessibility:** every field has a visible label; the wizard is fully keyboard-operable; works on mobile and desktop.
- **Data:** fictitious data only. No real personal data, documents, plates or credentials anywhere in the repo.

## Plan Phase Additions (Gate 2)
`plan.md` must also contain, when applicable:
- **Unit test candidates:** list the unit tests worth writing (business logic, validations, calculations, data mapping, critical interactions; never trivial rendering or getters), each with **what** it checks and **why** it matters, as a table (ID `UT-NN`, area, what, why). Table-driven tests state their example count. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. Developer agents write only approved unit tests; a regression test for a bug found after Gate 2 (review finding or Gate 3 correction) is allowed and must be named in its task.
- **E2E candidates:** list only critical flows that deserve an e2e test, each with a one-line justification. The human marks each one **Approved** or **Rejected** at Gate 2. The `e2e-tester` agent runs only for approved candidates.
- **Design options:** for every client-facing view, 2–3 design options based on the `ui-ux-guidelines` skill, with a recommendation. The human picks one at Gate 2.
- **ADRs:** every architectural decision gets an ADR in `docs/adr/` (context, alternatives, consequences), linked from `plan.md`.
- **Revisions:** when the human rejects or corrects the plan at Gate 2, append an entry to a `## Revisions` section at the end of `plan.md`: date, what the human asked to change, and what changed. Never delete entries.

## Asking the Human

# Angular conventions (Angular 22, standalone, zoneless)

## Folder layout (feature-first)
```
frontend/src/app/
  core/                 # app-wide singletons: country context, http, error handling
  shared/ui/            # reusable presentational components (no business logic)
  features/<feature>/   # one folder per feature, e.g. country-selection, quote-form, plan-list, summary
    <feature>.page.ts   # routed container component
    components/         # presentational components of this feature
    data/               # API service + models (*.model.ts) + mappers
    state/              # signal-based store for the feature, if needed
    *.spec.ts           # tests next to the code they test
```

## Components
- Standalone only, `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`, no NgModules.
- `input()`, `output()`, `model()` signal APIs; `inject()` instead of constructor injection.
- Templates use `@if`, `@for` (always with `track`), `@switch`. No `*ngIf` / `*ngFor`.
- Container (page) components talk to services/state; presentational components only receive inputs and emit outputs.
- Every async view handles three states: loading, error (with retry), empty.

## State
- `signal()` / `computed()` for state; `linkedSignal()` / `resource()` / `httpResource()` when they simplify async data.
- RxJS only where streams are genuinely needed (e.g. debounced input). Convert at the edge with `toSignal()`.
- Wizard state that must survive back-navigation or refresh lives in one store per wizard, persisted to `sessionStorage` through a single persistence helper. Never store tokens there.

## HTTP and contracts
- Call only relative URLs (`/api/...`). No hosts, no tokens, no `environment.ts` secrets.
- Strapi responses are mapped to app models in `data/*.mapper.ts`; components never see raw Strapi shapes.
- Models mirror the Strapi schema (source of truth). Any schema change updates the model in the same commit.

## Forms
- Typed Reactive Forms (`FormGroup<{...}>`, `nonNullable`) or Signal Forms if stable in the installed version — decided once in the plan, then consistent.
- Dynamic form: config from CMS → typed field descriptors → validators built by a pure function (`buildValidators(field)`) that is unit-tested per rule.
- Error messages come from configuration, shown next to the field, linked with `aria-describedby`.

## Accessibility (mandatory)
- Every control has a visible `<label for>`; help text and errors linked via `aria-describedby`; invalid fields get `aria-invalid="true"`.
- The whole wizard is operable by keyboard; on step change, move focus to the step heading.
- Use native elements (`button`, `input`, `select`) before ARIA roles.

## Styling
- BEM class names: `block__element--modifier`. SCSS per component; design tokens as CSS custom properties in `styles.scss`.
- Mobile-first; layouts must work from 320px width.

## Testing
- Vitest unit tests for: validators, mappers, price rules, stores, critical component interactions.
- No tests for styles, static templates or scaffolding.
- Name tests after requirements: `describe('US-01 · FR-003 vehicle year range', ...)`.
- Prefer testing pure functions; for components use `TestBed` with harness-free DOM queries by role/label.

# UI/UX guidelines

Visual language derived from research of the public car-insurance sites of a reference LatAm insurer operating in Colombia and Chile (2026-11-21). We reuse its **patterns and token values**, never its assets: no third-party logos, fonts or images in the repo. The product is a fictitious insurtech with its own text wordmark.

## 1. Design tokens

Defined once as CSS custom properties in `frontend/src/styles.scss`. Components use tokens only — no raw hex values.

```scss
:root {
  /* Brand */
  --color-brand: #0033a0;          /* navy: header, wordmark, info */
  --color-action: #2d6df6;         /* buttons, links, plan names */
  --color-action-hover: #26328c;
  --color-cta: #e3e829;            /* main CTA background only */
  --color-cta-hover: #d7de17;
  --color-on-cta: #26328c;         /* text on yellow */
  --color-accent: #00aec7;         /* DECORATIVE ONLY, never text (2.7:1) */

  /* Text & surfaces */
  --color-text: #1c1c24;
  --color-text-muted: #53565a;
  --color-surface: #ffffff;
  --color-surface-alt: #f8f8f8;    /* cards */
  --color-surface-highlight: #dfeaff; /* recommended plan, badges */
  --color-border: #cdced9;
  --color-disabled-bg: #e7e7e7;
  --color-disabled-text: #666666;   /* 4.6:1 on disabled-bg (Sura's #878789 was 2.9:1) */

  /* Status (fg / bg) */
  --color-error: #d12d35;   --color-error-bg: #fff4f3;
  --color-success: #067014; --color-success-bg: #def6de;
  --color-warning: #ed8b00; --color-warning-bg: #fff5ec;
  --color-info: #0033a0;    --color-info-bg: #e0eaff;

  /* Spacing (4px base) */
  --space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 12px; --space-4: 16px;
  --space-6: 24px; --space-8: 32px; --space-12: 48px;

  /* Radius */
  --radius-sm: 8px;      /* inputs */
  --radius-md: 16px;     /* cards */
  --radius-pill: 999px;  /* buttons, badges */

  /* Elevation */
  --shadow-card: 0 4px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.16);
  --shadow-soft: 0 8px 25px rgba(83, 89, 144, 0.07);
  --focus-ring: 0 0 0 4px rgba(0, 56, 255, 0.22);
}
```

## 2. Typography

- **Font:** Figtree from the Google Fonts CDN, only the weights we use, with `display=swap`:
  ```html
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Figtree:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  ```
- **Fallback (lightweight, no download):** `--font-family: 'Figtree', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;`
- **Scale (mobile → desktop):**

| Role | Size | Weight | Color |
|------|------|--------|-------|
| Price / hero heading | 32px → 48px | 700 | `--color-text` |
| Step heading (`h1`) | 24px → 32px | 700 | `--color-brand` |
| Section / card title | 20px | 700 | `--color-action` |
| Body | 16px, line-height 1.5 | 400 | `--color-text` |
| Label, badge, helper | 14px | 500 | `--color-text-muted` |

- Never below 14px. Blue text (`--color-action`) only at ≥16px.

## 3. Component recipes (BEM)

Each component defines: default, hover, focus-visible, disabled and (if applicable) error/selected states.

**Button** — `.button`, `.button--cta`, `.button--primary`, `.button--secondary`
- Pill (`--radius-pill`), min-height 48px, padding `--space-3 --space-6`, 16px / 700.
- `--cta`: yellow bg, navy text. One per screen: the step's main action (Continue, Pay).
- `--primary`: action-blue bg, white text, hover `--color-action-hover`.
- `--secondary`: white bg, 1px navy border (Back, Edit).
- Disabled: `--color-disabled-bg` / `--color-disabled-text` (≥ 4.5:1), plus `aria-disabled` or `disabled`. Loading: keep width, show spinner + "Procesando…", `aria-busy="true"`.

**Choice tile** — `.choice-tile`, `--selected`: large single-choice option (e.g. country). Native radio inside a `<label>`.
- Default: `--color-surface`, 2px `--color-border`, `--radius-md`, min-height 96px, flag above name, name 20px/700 `--color-text` (black, never brand or white).
- Hover: border `--color-action` only. Never a background change or dark fill.
- Selected: 2px `--color-action` border + bg `--color-surface-highlight` + check icon absolutely positioned in the top-right corner (not color alone; no extra text, so selecting causes no layout shift). The native radio announces the checked state.
- Focus: `--focus-ring`. All text states ≥ 4.5:1.

**Form field** — `.form-field`, `__label`, `__control`, `__help`, `__error`, `--invalid`
- Label above the control, 14px/500; required marked with `*` and announced (`required` attribute).
- Control (soft filled, chosen at US-01 Gate 2): min-height 52px, 16px text (prevents iOS zoom), `--color-surface-brand-soft` fill, 12px top radius, no side borders, 2px bottom line `--color-text-muted` (≥3:1 against the fill). Focus: bottom line `--color-action`, fill `--color-surface-field-focus` (`#e8f0ff`), plus `--focus-ring` on `:focus-visible`. Invalid: bottom line `--color-error`.
- Placeholder only as an example (`Ej: ABC123`), never as the label.
- Error: icon + text in `--color-error` below the control, `aria-describedby` linked, `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
- **Select** (`.select-field`): never the native option list. A `role="combobox"` trigger with the same soft-filled look and a chevron that rotates when open, plus a `role="listbox"` popup: white, 14px radius, `--shadow-card`, 6px padding; options 10px/12px padding, 10px radius, `--color-surface-brand-soft` for the active option, selected option bold `--color-on-cta` with a check icon. Keyboard per the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox: ↑/↓, Home/End, Enter/Space to pick, Esc to close, Tab to leave; `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`.
- Yes/No and short choices: segmented toggle built on native radio inputs (`.segmented`, `__option`, `--checked`).

**Form card** — `.form-card`: `--color-surface`, `--radius-md`, `--shadow-card`, padding `--space-6`, max-width 560px, centered. Title 20px/700 `--color-action`.

**Plan card** — `.plan-card`, `__badge`, `__radio`, `__name`, `__price`, `__section`, `__item`, `--recommended`, `--selected` (agreed at US-02 Gate 2)
- White `--color-surface`, 14px radius, padding `--space-4`/`--space-6`, 1px inset ring `--color-border`. No top stripe and no grey background.
- `--recommended`: a 5px `--color-brand` top border, a 1px brand ring, and a large `__badge` pill ("Recomendado" with a star icon; 16px bold text, an 18px icon, 6px × 18px padding; `--color-cta` bg, `--color-on-cta` text) centred **on the top border**. Only the first recommended plan in order.
- `--selected`: a `__radio` circle filled with `--color-action` and a white check, plus a 2px **inset** `--color-action` ring. No "Seleccionado" text: nothing may change size or position (no layout shift). The radio state is the non-colour cue.
- The cards share one CSS subgrid, so the name and description, the price (after a divider), Coberturas and Beneficios start on the same line in every card.
- Price: large, `--color-brand`, formatted in the country's currency with no decimals, followed by "/ mes". No text explaining how the price is calculated.
- Sections: Coberturas and Beneficios with check icons; an empty list is hidden.
- Selectable as a radio group, one choice only; the arrow keys move the choice.
- The "Continuar" pill is disabled (`--color-disabled-bg` / `--color-disabled-text`) until a plan is chosen, with no hint text.

**Stepper** — `.stepper`, `__step`, `--current`, `--done`: numbered steps with text labels in an `<ol>`, above the form card; current step has `aria-current="step"`. Current and done circles (32px): `--color-surface-highlight` fill, 2px `--color-action` ring, `--color-brand` number (check icon when done); upcoming: white, 1.5px `--color-border` ring, `--color-text-muted`. Current label bold `--color-brand`; connector lines 2px, `--color-action` up to a done step, else `--color-border`. On mobile show only the current circle + "Paso 2 de 3" + current label.

**Motion** — content loads with a skeleton, then items fade up 14px one by one (600ms `cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`, 110ms stagger), only on first render, never on validation re-renders. Popups open with a 160ms fade/slide. All of it is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**Summary block** — `.summary-section` with a title + "Editar" secondary link per section (data, vehicle, plan). Masked document shown as `•••• 5678`.

**States**
- **Loading:** skeletons shaped like the final content (cards, fields); `aria-busy` on the region.
- **Empty** (e.g. no plans): flat illustration or icon, friendly headline, one-line explanation, one action.
- **Error** (e.g. payment rejected, CMS down): `--color-error-bg` panel with icon, what happened, what to do, and a retry button. Never lose user data.
- **Success** (confirmation): `--color-success` check icon, headline, quote number prominent and copyable.

# Feature Specification: US-02 – Plan list

**Feature Branch**: `003-us-02-plan-list`

**Created**: 2026-11-22

**Status**: Approved (Gate 1) — 2026-11-22

**Input**: User story [US-02](../../docs/user-stories/US-02.md) (verbatim business story, the source of truth). Builds on [US-01](../002-us-01-policyholder-vehicle-form/spec.md), which provides the step 1 form, the tab's quote session (step 1 values and completion) and a step 2 placeholder at `/:country/quote/plans`. Architecture: [ADR 0001](../../docs/adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (Plan collection, currency on Country, limits of configurability), [ADR 0003](../../docs/adr/0003-bootstrap-grid-for-layouts.md) (layout), [ADR 0004](../../docs/adr/0004-dynamic-form-from-cms.md) (step 1 values by field key).

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-11-22

- Q: Which step 1 data drives the simulated price rule? → A: The policyholder's age and the vehicle's age: final price = base price × driver-age factor × vehicle-age factor (FR-005).
- Q: Can the business change the rule's factors from the content manager? → A: Yes, per country. The age bands and their factors are configured on the Country; the shape of the rule (age × vehicle) is fixed and documented (ADR 0001, limits of configurability).
- Q: Where is the currency configured? → A: On the Country only, with its number format, as ADR 0001 says; every plan uses its country's currency (FR-004).
- Q: What period does a price cover and what does a plan show? → A: Prices are monthly. Each plan shows only its final monthly price ("/ mes") (FR-004).
- Q (Gate 2, human design review): Should the page explain how the price is calculated? → A: No. The rule still applies, but the person doesn't need to know how the company estimates prices: no help text about it. The rule is documented as an explicit decision in the docs (ADR 0005), in the code and in the content manager (FR-004, FR-005).
- Q (Gate 2, human design review): What does "Continuar" do before a plan is chosen? → A: It is disabled until a plan is chosen, with no extra hint text (FR-008).

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - See the plans for my country (Priority: P1)

A person who completed step 1 sees the plans offered in their country, in the order the business chose, each with its name, short description, price, coverages and benefits.

**Why this priority**: Without plans there is nothing to choose; it is the core of the quote.

**Independent Test**: With plans configured for Colombia and Chile, complete step 1 in each country and check that step 2 shows only that country's active, published plans, in order, with prices in the country's currency.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I completed step 1, **When** I reach the plans step, **Then** I see only the active and published plans for my country, in the configured order.
2. **Given** a plan, **When** I view it, **Then** I see its name, short description, final price in my country's currency and format, its coverages and its benefits.
3. **Given** a plan is inactive, unpublished or belongs to another country, **When** I view the list, **Then** it is not shown.

---

### User Story 2 - Spot the recommended plan (Priority: P2)

The business marks one plan as recommended, and the person sees it highlighted.

**Why this priority**: It guides the choice, but the list works without it.

**Independent Test**: Mark one Chilean plan as recommended, reload step 2 for Chile: that plan is visually distinguished and announced as recommended.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a plan is marked as recommended, **When** I view the plan list, **Then** that plan is visually distinguished from the others, and the distinction is not conveyed by colour alone.
2. **Given** no plan is marked as recommended, **When** I view the list, **Then** no plan is highlighted.

---

### User Story 3 - Choose one plan and continue (Priority: P1)

The person selects exactly one plan and moves on to the summary.

**Why this priority**: The quote cannot finish without a chosen plan.

**Independent Test**: Select a plan, then another: only the last one is marked. Press "Continuar": the summary step opens. Go back: the chosen plan is still marked.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** I am on the plan list, **When** I select a plan, **Then** it is marked as chosen and any previously chosen plan is not.
2. **Given** a plan is chosen, **When** I press "Continuar", **Then** I move on to the summary step.
3. **Given** no plan is chosen, **When** I view the list, **Then** "Continuar" is disabled.
4. **Given** I chose a plan, **When** I come back to step 2 from the summary or reload the tab, **Then** the same plan is still chosen, if it is still offered.
5. **Given** I use only the keyboard or a screen reader, **When** I choose a plan, **Then** I can reach, choose and confirm it, and I hear which plan is chosen.

---

### User Story 4 - Be told when there are no plans (Priority: P2)

When the business has no active plans for a country, the person is told so instead of seeing an empty page.

**Why this priority**: An empty page would look broken and lose the person.

**Independent Test**: Deactivate every plan of a country and reach step 2: a clear message explains that no plans are available, with a way back.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** there are no active plans for my country, **When** I reach the plans step, **Then** I see a message explaining that no plans are available, and "Continuar" is not offered.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Content service fails**: step 2 shows an error with a retry action, like step 1 (US-01 FR-010).
- **Step 1 data no longer valid** (the business changed a field or rule after the person continued, review R-19): step 2 re-checks the saved step 1 values against the current fields and sends the person back to step 1 when they are not valid.
- **Chosen plan no longer offered** (deactivated, unpublished or removed): the choice is dropped, and the person must choose again.
- **Step 1 edited after choosing a plan**: the plan stays chosen and its price is recalculated with the new data.
- **More than one plan marked as recommended**: only the first one in the configured order is highlighted.
- **Plan saved without a country**: the content manager rejects it, as for form fields (ADR 0001 mitigation).
- **Plan with no coverages or no benefits**: shown without that list; never an empty heading.
- **Price adjustment needs a step 1 value that the country does not ask for**, or no band covers the age: that factor does not apply (factor 1).
- **Overlapping bands** configured by mistake: the first band in its configured order wins.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The business team MUST be able to configure each plan per country with: name, short description, base price, coverages, benefits, order, recommended flag, active status and country, and publish or unpublish it, without code changes.
- **FR-002**: Step 2 MUST show only the plans of the active country that are published and active, sorted by their configured order.
- **FR-003**: Each plan MUST show its name, short description, final price, coverages and benefits.
- **FR-004**: Prices are monthly. Each plan MUST show only its final monthly price, followed by "/ mes", in the active country's currency and number format (Colombian pesos for Colombia, Chilean pesos for Chile), with no decimals. The currency and format are configured once on the country, never on a plan. The page does not explain how the price is calculated.
- **FR-005**: The final price MUST be the base price × the driver-age factor × the vehicle-age factor, rounded to a whole peso. Each factor comes from the age bands configured on the active country (an age range and its factor); the policyholder's age and the vehicle's age come from step 1. The rule is simulated, and it is documented as an explicit decision in the docs, in the code and in the content manager's field descriptions, but not shown to the person. The same inputs MUST always give the same price.
- **FR-006**: A plan marked as recommended MUST be visually distinguished and announced as recommended to assistive technology. At most one plan is highlighted (see Edge Cases).
- **FR-007**: The person MUST be able to choose exactly one plan; choosing another replaces the choice. The choice MUST be visible and announced.
- **FR-008**: "Continuar" MUST be disabled until a plan is chosen; once a plan is chosen, it moves to the summary step.
- **FR-009**: The chosen plan MUST be saved in the tab's session and restored when the person returns to step 2 or reloads, while the plan is still offered.
- **FR-010**: Step 2 MUST show loading, empty ("no plans available") and error (with retry) states. The empty state offers a way back to step 1.
- **FR-011**: Step 2 MUST be reachable only with a complete and still valid step 1 (US-01 guard, plus the re-check in Edge Cases).
- **FR-012**: The summary step MUST exist as a placeholder with a "Volver" action to step 2, until US-03 replaces it.
- **FR-013**: The plan list MUST be fully keyboard-operable and work on mobile (320 px) and desktop.
- **FR-014**: The seed MUST provide fictitious plans: 3 for Colombia and 3 for Chile, each with coverages and benefits, one recommended per country, plus one inactive plan to show filtering, and the price factors of each country (see Assumptions).

### Key Entities

- **Plan**: one offer in one country. Attributes: name, short description, base price, coverages (list), benefits (list), order, recommended, active, country, publication status.
- **Country** (from US-00/US-01): gains its **currency**, **number format**, **driver-age bands** and **vehicle-age bands** (each band: from age, to age, factor) in this story.
- **Quote session** (from US-01): now also holds the chosen plan.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A plan published, reordered, highlighted or deactivated by the business team is reflected on step 2 after a reload, with no deployment, in 100% of cases.
- **SC-002**: 100% of shown prices use the country's currency and format, and match the documented rule for the given step 1 data.
- **SC-003**: A person can compare the plans and choose one in under 1 minute.
- **SC-004**: The chosen plan is still chosen in 100% of returns to step 2 and reloads, while it is offered.
- **SC-005**: The whole step can be completed using only the keyboard, on mobile (320 px) and desktop.

## Assumptions

- Copy is in Spanish. Plan texts come from the content manager; state messages and button texts are fixed application texts.
- **Seeded price factors (same for both countries, editable per country):** driver age under 25: 1.20; 25–65: 1.00; over 65: 1.15. Vehicle age 0–5 years: 1.00; 6–10: 1.10; 11–20: 1.20. Ages are whole years on the current date. It is a simulation, not a real tariff.
- The summary step (US-03) does not exist yet, so it is a placeholder (FR-012). Data stays in the tab's session and is never sent to a server.
- Data is fictitious: plan names, prices, coverages and benefits are invented.

## Conflicts with ADR 0001 *(resolved at clarify)*

- **Currency:** the story lists currency as a plan attribute; ADR 0001 keeps it only on Country. Resolved: Country only (FR-004).
- **Price rule:** resolved as a fixed, documented rule shape with its factors configured per country (FR-005), consistent with ADR 0001's limits of configurability.
# Implementation Plan: US-02 – Plan list

**Branch**: `003-us-02-plan-list` | **Date**: 2026-11-22 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) (Approved Gate 1)

**Status**: Approved (Gate 2) — 2026-11-22

**Testing**: Vitest (frontend and cms) for the approved UT candidates only; Playwright for the approved E2E candidates only

## Constitution Check

|-----------|--------|
| KISS / ask before over-engineering | ✅ A pure price function, no rule engine (ADR 0005); fixed badge text (R11) |
| No new dependency (§3.2) | ✅ Only `swiper`, requested and approved by the human at Gate 2 |
| Feature-first, cohesive files | ✅ New `features/plan-list/` (page, card, data, pricing) |
| High-value tests only | ✅ Only the UT candidates the human approves below |

| Breaking API contract (§3.3) | ✅ Additive: a new endpoint and new Country fields |
| No personal data sent | ✅ The price is calculated in the browser (R1) |

# Research — US-02 Plan list

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md)

## R1 — Where the price is calculated
- **Decision:** in Angular, as a pure function `simulatePrice(basePrice, driverAge, vehicleAge, country)` in `features/plan-list/pricing/`. The bands come from the Country (CMS), and the ages come from the step 1 values saved in the tab.
- **Rationale:**
  - The spec keeps step 1 data in the tab and never sends it to a server (Assumptions). A server endpoint would need the birth date.
  - A pure function always gives the same price for the same inputs (FR-005), and a table of examples tests it.
- **Alternatives:**
  - A Strapi custom endpoint: it sends personal data and adds code.
  - Factors hard-coded in Angular: this breaks clarify Q2, which makes them editable per country.
  - See [ADR 0005](../../docs/adr/0005-simulated-price-rule-age-bands.md).

## R2 — How the age bands are stored
- **Decision:**
  - Country gets two repeatable components, `driverAgeBands` and `vehicleAgeBands`. Both use the type `pricing.age-band` (`fromAge`, `toAge`, `factor`).
  - The band order in the admin is the lookup order: the first band that covers the age wins (Edge Cases).
- **Rationale:** editors see the bands next to the country's currency. There is no new collection and no relation to forget.
- **Alternatives:**
  - A `PriceFactor` collection: one more relation that can be left empty.
  - A JSON field: no validation in the admin.

## R3 — Which step 1 values drive the price
- **Decision:** the field keys `birthDate` and `vehicleYear` (ADR 0004: keys are stable, and the price rule uses them).
  - **Driver age:** whole years on today's date, the same calculation as `legalAge`.
  - **Vehicle age:** the current year − `vehicleYear`, never below 0.
  - **Factor 1:** applies when the value is missing or can't be read, or when no band covers the age (Edge Cases).
- **Rationale:** labels change but keys do not. Both keys exist in the CO and CL seeds.

## R4 — Currency and number format
- **Decision:**
  - Country gains `currency` (ISO 4217, `^[A-Z]{3}$`) and `numberLocale` (BCP 47, `^[a-z]{2}-[A-Z]{2}$`).
  - Angular formats the price with `Intl.NumberFormat(numberLocale, { style: 'currency', currency, maximumFractionDigits: 0, minimumFractionDigits: 0 })` and adds " / mes" (FR-004).
  - Seed: CO `COP` / `es-CO`, CL `CLP` / `es-CL`, PE `PEN` / `es-PE`.
- **Rationale:**
  - `Intl` ships with the browser: no new dependency, and no Angular locale data to register.
  - COP has 2 decimals by default, so 0 decimals is forced.
- **Alternatives:** Angular `CurrencyPipe`. It needs `registerLocaleData` for each country, which hard-codes the country list.

## R5 — Existing databases
- **Decision:**
  - A bootstrap backfill, like the US-01 `legalAge` one: for each seeded country code, it sets `currency`, `numberLocale` and the bands only when they are empty. It never overwrites an edited value.
  - Plans are seeded only when the Plan collection is empty.

## R6 — Plan save check
- **Decision:**
  - Turn the US-01 Document Service middleware into one module that covers both content types:
    - **FormField:** needs a country, and its key is unique per country.
    - **Plan:** needs a country.
  - `readCountryPayload` is reused as is.
  - Message: "El plan debe tener un país."
- **Rationale:**
  - The ADR 0001 mitigation lives in one place.
  - The admin payload quirks fixed in T028 are already handled.

## R7 — Published plans only
- **Decision:**
  - The Plan `find` controller forces `status: 'published'`, as FormField does (US-01 R3).
  - Public gets only Plan `find`.

## R8 — Re-checking step 1 on step 2 (review R-19)
- **Decision:** `step1CompleteGuard` becomes async. Besides `step1Completed`, it loads the country's form fields and checks the saved values with the same validators as step 1:
  - It runs `buildValidators` on a throw-away `FormGroup`.
  - Saved select values go through US-01's `restoredValue` rule first.
  - **Values invalid:** the guard clears `step1Completed` and redirects to step 1, where the errors show (US-01 FR-005).
  - **Fields fail to load:** it redirects to step 1, which shows its error and retry. No value is lost.
- **Rationale:** both steps use one set of rules, so validation is not duplicated.

## R9 — Chosen plan in the session
- **Decision:** the chosen plan is stored as `data.planId` (the plan's `documentId`) in `quote-session`.
  - `saveStep1` keeps it, so the price is recalculated (Edge Cases).
  - `discardData` and a country change drop it.
  - On load, a `planId` that is not in the list is removed (FR-009).

## R10 — Selection control
- **Decision:** a native radio group, per the plan-card recipe:
  - A `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, and one `<input type="radio">` inside each card's `<label>`.
  - The arrow keys move between plans.
  - The chosen card shows "Seleccionado" with a check icon.
  - "Continuar" is disabled until a plan is chosen, with no hint text (FR-008, Gate 2).
  - Selection needs no text: the custom radio and the ring change, and nothing moves (no layout shift).
- **Alternatives:** buttons with `aria-pressed`. They have no arrow-key behaviour and need more ARIA to get right.

## R11 — Recommended badge
- **Decision:**
  - The mapper highlights only the first `recommended` plan in order (Edge Cases).
  - The badge text is fixed, "Recomendado". The radio label adds a visually hidden ", plan recomendado" (FR-006).
- **Alternatives:** badge text from the CMS. The recipe allows it, but the story doesn't need it, so it is not added.

## R12 — Where the price rule is documented
- **Decision:** the rule is not shown to the person (Gate 2). It is documented in three places:
  - [ADR 0005](../../docs/adr/0005-simulated-price-rule-age-bands.md).
  - A doc comment on `simulatePrice`, linking ADR 0005.
  - The Strapi `description` of the Country band fields and of the `pricing.age-band` component, so editors see what a factor does.

## R13 — Plan slider (below 992 px)
- **Decision:** `swiper` (core API, with the Navigation, Pagination, A11y and Keyboard modules), as the human asked at Gate 2.
  - Created in `afterNextRender` only when the viewport is below 992 px, and destroyed above that. From 992 px the same cards sit in a 3-column grid.
  - `loop: false`, no autoplay, `slidesPerView` about 1.2 (mobile) and 2.2 (tablet), centred on the recommended plan.
  - Arrows and dots are real buttons with Spanish labels.
  - Choosing a plan with the arrow keys calls `slideTo`.
  - The only motion is the step 1 load animation, which is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Trade-off:** slides are separate boxes, so rows align exactly only in the desktop grid (CSS subgrid). In the slider the cards keep equal heights.
- **Alternatives:** the CSS scroll-snap slider from the mockup, which needs no dependency. The human preferred Swiper.
# Data model — US-02 Plan list

The source of truth is `cms/src/api/**/schema.json`. The Angular models in `features/plan-list/data/` and `core/country/` mirror it, and change in the same commit.

## Plan (new collection `api::plan.plan`, draft & publish)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|-----------|------|-------|
| `name` | string | required |
| `shortDescription` | string | required, maxLength 160 |
| `basePrice` | integer | required, min 0 (whole pesos, monthly) |
| `coverages` | component `plan.item`, repeatable | may be empty |
| `benefits` | component `plan.item`, repeatable | may be empty |
| `order` | integer | required, min 1 |
| `recommended` | boolean | default false |
| `active` | boolean | required, default true |
| `country` | relation many-to-one → Country | required by the save check (R6) |

**Component `plan.item`:** `text` (string, required, maxLength 120).

## Country (changes)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|-----------|------|-------|
| `currency` | string | required, `^[A-Z]{3}$` |
| `numberLocale` | string | required, `^[a-z]{2}-[A-Z]{2}$` |
| `driverAgeBands` | component `pricing.age-band`, repeatable | order = lookup order |
| `vehicleAgeBands` | component `pricing.age-band`, repeatable | order = lookup order |

**Component `pricing.age-band`:**
- `fromAge`: integer, required, min 0.
- `toAge`: integer, required, min 0.
- `factor`: decimal, required, min 0.01.

A band covers an age when `fromAge ≤ age ≤ toAge`.

The schema `description` of `driverAgeBands`, `vehicleAgeBands` and `pricing.age-band` explains the rule to editors: "Monthly price = base price × driver-age factor × vehicle-age factor. The first band that covers the age applies; no band → factor 1. Not shown to customers (ADR 0005)."

**Seed bands (both countries):**

| Band | Ages | Factor |
|------|------|--------|
| Driver | 0–24 | 1.20 |
| Driver | 25–65 | 1.00 |
| Driver | 66–120 | 1.15 |
| Vehicle | 0–5 | 1.00 |
| Vehicle | 6–10 | 1.10 |
| Vehicle | 11–20 | 1.20 |

**Seed plans (fictitious):**

| Country | Plan | Base price | Notes |
|---------|------|-----------|-------|
| CO | Básico | 89.000 | |
| CO | Plus | 145.000 | recommended |
| CO | Total | 210.000 | |
| CO | Clásico | 99.000 | inactive |
| CL | Esencial | 24.990 | |
| CL | Plus | 39.990 | recommended |
| CL | Full | 59.990 | |

Each plan has 2 to 5 coverages and 1 to 3 benefits.

## Angular models

- **`Country`** gains `currency: string`, `numberLocale: string`, `driverAgeBands: AgeBand[]` and `vehicleAgeBands: AgeBand[]`.
  - The mapper drops a band with `fromAge > toAge` or `factor ≤ 0`.
  - Missing bands become `[]`, which gives factor 1.
- **`Plan`** has `id` (the documentId), `name`, `shortDescription`, `basePrice`, `coverages: string[]`, `benefits: string[]` and `highlighted: boolean`.
  - `highlighted` is true only for the first recommended plan in order.
  - A DTO without a finite `basePrice ≥ 0` is dropped.
- **`PlanOffer`** (view model) has `plan`, `finalPrice` (integer) and `formattedPrice` ("$ 145.000 / mes").

## Quote session (`sessionStorage['quote-session']`)

```text
{ countryCode, data: { step1: {…}, step1Completed?: true, planId?: string } }
```

- New methods: `savePlan(id)`, `readPlanId()`, `clearPlan()`.
- `saveStep1` keeps `planId`.
- `discardData` and `start(otherCountry)` drop it.

## Price rule (FR-005, ADR 0005)

```text
finalPrice = round(basePrice × factor(driverAge, driverAgeBands) × factor(vehicleAge, vehicleAgeBands))
factor(age, bands) = first band with fromAge ≤ age ≤ toAge → its factor; none, or age unknown → 1
```

Example: base 145.000, driver aged 22 (factor 1.20), vehicle 8 years old (factor 1.10) → 191.400.
# Contract — Plans API and Country additions (US-02)

## `GET /api/plans` (Public: `find`)

```text
/api/plans?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&filters[active][$eq]=true&sort=order:asc
  &populate[coverages]=true&populate[benefits]=true&pagination[pageSize]=100
```

- Always returns published entries only: the controller forces `status=published` (R7). Unpublished plans, inactive plans and other countries' plans never come back (FR-002).
- Response item:

```json
{ "id": 1, "documentId": "abc", "name": "Plus", "shortDescription": "Lo esencial y más.",
  "basePrice": 145000, "order": 2, "recommended": true, "active": true,
  "coverages": [{ "id": 3, "text": "Responsabilidad civil" }],
  "benefits": [{ "id": 7, "text": "Grúa 24/7" }] }
```

- **Errors:** any non-2xx response shows the step 2 error state with a retry (FR-010).

## `GET /api/countries` (Public: `find`, existing) — additions

- The existing query also requests `populate[driverAgeBands]=true&populate[vehicleAgeBands]=true`.
- Each item gains these fields:
  - `currency`
  - `numberLocale`
  - `driverAgeBands`, e.g. `[{ "fromAge": 0, "toAge": 24, "factor": 1.2 }]`
  - `vehicleAgeBands`, in the same shape

## Save check (Document Service middleware)

- Creating, updating or publishing a Plan without a country fails with HTTP 400 "El plan debe tener un país."
- An admin save that leaves the country untouched passes (US-01 T028).

## Change type

Additive: a new endpoint and new Country fields (constitution §3.3).
# Contract — Application routes (US-02 changes)

This adds to the [US-01 routes contract](../../002-us-01-policyholder-vehicle-form/contracts/routes.md).

| Address | Shows | Spec |
|---------|-------|------|
| `/:country/quote/plans` | The plan list, replacing the placeholder: loading, list, empty and error states | FR-002–FR-010 |
| `/:country/quote/plans` when step 1 is not complete or no longer valid | Redirect to `/:country/quote`, where the errors show | FR-011, R8 |
| `/:country/quote/summary` | A summary placeholder with "Volver" to the plans (until US-03) | FR-012 |
| `/:country/quote/summary` with no chosen plan | Redirect to `/:country/quote/plans` | FR-008 |

Rules:
- **"Continuar":**
  - With a chosen plan, it goes to `summary`.
  - Without one, it is disabled (FR-008).
- **Empty state:** it offers "Volver a tus datos" (back to step 1) and no "Continuar" (FR-010, User Story 4).
- **Focus:** on each step change, focus moves to the step heading.
# 0005 — Simulated price rule with age bands on Country

- **Status:** Accepted (Gate 2, US-02 — 2026-11-22)
- **Date:** 2026-11-22
- **Related:** US-02, ADR 0001 ("Limits of configurability"), ADR 0004 (field keys), `specs/003-us-02-plan-list/research.md` (R1–R4)

## Context and problem

Step 2 shows each plan's monthly price adjusted by step 1 data (US-02 FR-005). The clarify answers fix the rule as **base price × driver-age factor × vehicle-age factor**, rounded to a whole peso.
- The factors are editable per country from Strapi.
- The currency and number format live only on the Country.

Step 1 data (the birth date) stays in the tab and is never sent to a server. The rule is a simulation, not a real tariff, but it must be deterministic and documented.

## Decision drivers

- The business edits the factors without a deployment (clarify Q2).
- Personal data never leaves the browser (spec Assumptions).
- The same inputs always give the same price (FR-005), and the rule is easy to test.
- KISS: no rule engine, and no new dependency.

## Considered options

1. **Age bands on Country, price calculated in Angular** with a pure function.
2. **A Strapi custom endpoint** `POST /api/quotes/price` that receives the ages and returns the prices.
3. **A generic formula** stored in the CMS (JSON or an expression) and run by Angular.
4. **Factors hard-coded** in Angular per country.

## Decision

Chosen option: **1**.
- Country gets two repeatable components, `driverAgeBands` and `vehicleAgeBands`, with entries `{ fromAge, toAge, factor }`.
- Angular calculates `round(basePrice × driverFactor × vehicleFactor)`:
  - The ages come from the step 1 keys `birthDate` and `vehicleYear`.
  - The first band covering the age wins.
  - A missing value, or no matching band, gives factor 1.
- The price is formatted with `Intl.NumberFormat(country.numberLocale, { style: 'currency', currency: country.currency })` with 0 decimals.

**The rule is not explained to the person** (Gate 2): the page shows only the final monthly price. It is documented as an explicit decision in:
- this ADR;
- a doc comment on `simulatePrice` that links here;
- the Strapi `description` of the band fields and of the `pricing.age-band` component, so editors know what a factor does.

This meets every driver: editors change numbers in the admin, and nothing personal is sent. The function is pure and has a table of examples.

## Consequences

- **Positive:**
  - Factors, bands, currency and format are content.
  - A new country only needs its bands.
  - The rule is visible in one small, tested function.
- **Negative / trade-offs:**
  - The *shape* of the rule (two age factors, multiplied) is code. A new factor, such as the vehicle make, needs a developer. This is consistent with ADR 0001's limits of configurability.
  - The price is only a display price. It is not a server-trusted quote: anyone can change it in their own browser. That is acceptable for a simulation with no payment.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - US-03 shows the same `finalPrice` in the summary, reusing the function.
  - A real tariff would move the price to the server (option 2), which would also need a consent and privacy decision.

## Pros and cons of the options

### 1. Bands on Country, Angular calculates
- Good: no personal data sent; deterministic; editable; no new endpoint.
- Bad: the price can't be trusted server-side.

### 2. Strapi endpoint
- Good: one authoritative price; the rule is hidden.
- Bad: the birth date goes to the server; it needs a custom route, a permission, and error handling; it is overkill for a simulation.

### 3. Generic formula in the CMS
- Good: the most flexible.
- Bad: editors write code without validation; it needs an evaluator, which brings a dependency or a security risk; it is over-engineered.

### 4. Hard-coded factors
- Good: the simplest.
- Bad: it breaks clarify Q2 and ADR 0001 ("no country data hardcoded in Angular").

## Review round 1 for US-02: Changes requested

There are 2 Major, 11 Minor and 1 Nit findings. I recorded all four known items as findings, since I confirmed each one: R-03, R-04, R-05 and R-06.

Checks I ran myself, all passing:
- `npm --prefix frontend run verify`: 179 tests in 18 files.
- `npm --prefix cms run build`.
- `npm --prefix cms test`: 37 tests.

I did not run E2E.

### Major
- **R-01 — `cms/src/seed/countries.ts:56-79`. The pricing backfill overwrites editor data and publishes drafts.**
  - It runs on every boot and treats an empty band list as missing. An editor who deliberately removes every band (the spec allows this: no band → factor 1) gets the seed bands back on each restart.
  - It writes with `strapi.documents().update({…, status: 'published'})`. In Strapi 5 that always writes the draft and then publishes the whole draft (I checked `@strapi/core/.../document-service/repository.js:394-438`). Any unpublished editor change on that country goes live.
  - The US-01 `backfillLegalAge` avoids this on purpose by using `db.query`.
  - Fix: only backfill rows that predate US-02 (for example, when `currency` is missing), and don't publish drafts.
- **R-02 — `step1-complete.guard.ts:36-38` with `step1-form.page.ts:115-141`. Step 1 shows nothing after the guard's re-check fails.**
  - Errors only appear when a field is touched or the form was submitted, and neither is true on a fresh load. The person is sent back with no message and no focus on the bad field.
  - This contradicts the routes contract ("where the errors show") and research R8.
  - Fix: pass a one-shot flag so step 1 runs its invalid-submit path, plus a named regression test.

### Minor
- **R-03:** commit `699548d` doesn't build on its own (the route still imports the deleted placeholder until `6888fd0`).
- **R-04:** the `anyComponentStyle` budget went up to 9/12 kB for every component, only for the Swiper CSS, and nothing records why.
- **R-05:** the price text reads "$ 145.000/ mes" because the two spans touch. That text is the radio's `aria-describedby`, and the E2E tests hide it by normalising the gap.
- **R-06:** the accessible name is "Plus , plan recomendado", and the E2E regex accepts the stray space.
- **R-07:** the slider dots are Swiper's default `span role=button`, not real buttons as R13 says. Their tap area is 24×48 px, below the 48×48 px minimum.
- **R-08:** under reduced motion, Swiper's 300 ms slide transition still runs.
- **R-09:** the whole card is a `<label>` that contains `<ul>`/`<li>`, which is invalid HTML.
- **R-10:** the UT-09 test copies the "effective country" logic into a helper, so the real `checkPlan` code never runs in tests.
- **R-11:** UT-01 never checks ages 5 or 10, although the test names say "5 and 6" and "10 and 11". "No band covers the age" is only tested with an empty band list.
- **R-12:** a country with no currency throws a `RangeError` in `Intl.NumberFormat`, and step 2 breaks with no error state. This can happen because the backfill only fills CO, CL and PE.
- **R-13:** the 3-column grid and the skeleton grid are laid out in component SCSS, not Bootstrap. The subgrid is a fair exception for the track, but it isn't recorded, and the skeleton has no such reason.

### Nit
- **R-14:** the US-01 SC-002 guard suite was renamed to US-02 and one of its cases was deleted, so US-01 traceability is lost.

### What conforms
- The price rule matches ADR 0005, including inclusive band edges, first band wins, and factor 1 for null ages.
- The guards: every `inject()` runs before the first `await`, and `planChosenGuard` works.
- The `planId` session lifecycle.
- Plan `find` is forced to published, and Public gets only `plan.find`.
- `seedPlans` is idempotent.
- Swiper is created and destroyed correctly, with no loop, no autoplay, and controls only in slider mode.
- Only tokens are used.
- All of UT-01…UT-10 and E2E-3/E2E-4 exist, and there are no unapproved tests.
- The Strapi schemas match the Angular models.
- There are no tokens or hosts in the frontend, and all data is fictitious.

The full review, with fix suggestions and manual checks for the human, is in `C:\Users\Quijote\Documents\insurance-multiregion-app\specs\003-us-02-plan-list\review.md`.
